topics.topic: Authoritative complete dependency inventory and factory admission evidence
questions: What generated release artifact is the authoritative complete list of runtime dependencies, exact versions and digests?
What factory evidence proves that the generated inventory includes every runtime import and all required non-package dependencies before a release is made?
How will factory checks construct and verify the complete dependency declaration, including transitive packages, Python and the base image, before admitting a release?

quotes:
A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with
its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of
its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM
Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system
libraries and the store's engine. Tools used only to build or test are not
dependencies of the running instance.

Rules 1–4 are kept by the release process and its installation, which
Registry does not manage (00_product.md, Explicit exclusions): they make
the release, name its dependencies and install them, and Registry's own
code reads none of it (owner, 2026-11-24). This decision therefore
declares no formal invariant of Registry: no note of a module and no
check of Registry's code can show what the installation does, and one
claimed here would be a false witness.

A release whose list misses a package the instance would import, the
Python version or the base image, or names any of them without an exact
version or a digest, is not made.
judgement.why: The authoritative generated inventory belongs to generation and the evidence that it is complete belongs to factory_checks, while State 5 has no Registry-module operation to specify because the texts expressly place A20 outside Registry.
options: Generate one canonical dependency lock containing Python, every direct and transitive package, and the base image.
Generate a package lock plus a separate release manifest for Python and the base image.
Generate an SBOM as the canonical inventory and attach the required distribution and image digests.
Resolve the complete runtime dependency graph from declared roots and compare it with the generated inventory.
Build the isolated release, inspect its installed runtime environment and compare that environment with the inventory.
Require both graph resolution and inspection of the built runtime environment.
Generate a locked dependency manifest from the resolved build and compare it with the packaged runtime inventory.
Treat a fully pinned manifest as the build input and reject any produced artifact whose runtime inventory differs.
consequences: One lock gives later checks one input but requires it to represent unlike dependency kinds.
Separate artifacts fit their ecosystems but require an explicit rule that their union is the complete release inventory.
An SBOM supports broader tooling but its schema must unambiguously identify exact runtime artifacts and exclude build-only tools.
Graph resolution is deterministic but can miss dependencies introduced outside the resolver's model.
Environment inspection checks the built result but needs a precise rule separating runtime dependencies from build and test tools.
Using both gives stronger evidence but adds two checks whose disagreement must reject the release.
Inventory-first checking detects undeclared resolved dependencies but requires deterministic inspection of every runtime artifact.
Manifest-first construction makes the declaration authoritative but requires the build to prove that no additional runtime dependency entered the artifact.

topics.topic: Installation-time enforcement of the admitted dependency set and digests
questions: At what installation boundary are dependency digests checked so that a mismatch prevents any Registry instance from starting?
How will deployment ensure that an installed and running instance contains exactly the admitted dependencies and cannot substitute or add runtime code?

quotes:
A running instance uses exactly those; installing a dependency whose digest
differs fails.

Rules 1–4 are kept by the release process and its installation, which
Registry does not manage (00_product.md, Explicit exclusions): they make
the release, name its dependencies and install them, and Registry's own
code reads none of it (owner, 2026-11-24). This decision therefore
declares no formal invariant of Registry: no note of a module and no
check of Registry's code can show what the installation does, and one
claimed here would be a false witness.

Installing the release fails when the digest differs for any one
dependency of each kind rule 1 names — a direct Python package, a
transitive one, the Python version and the base image — and no instance
of that release starts.

After an installation that succeeded, the dependencies the running
instance has are exactly the release's list, by name, version and
digest, nothing more.
judgement.why: The digest-check boundary, start gate, runtime isolation and prevention of added code are deployment choices outside State 5's public obligations between Registry modules.
options: The installer fetches every named artifact by digest and refuses before creating a runnable installation on any mismatch.
Deployment installs a factory-built immutable image and verifies only that image's digest against the admitted release.
Deployment verifies the image digest and also verifies an embedded inventory against the installed Python and package artifacts before enabling the process.
Install every artifact from a digest-verified locked set into an isolated runtime and verify the resulting inventory before start.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
